claim: Transfer between human tasks tracks shared components: gains are larger for similar than dissimilar tasks (Thorndike and Woodworth 1901) and production-rule overlap predicts skill transfer between editors (Singley and Anderson 1985, N=24).
agent_test: Tag each stored lesson with its class and shared-step signature; test same-class vs cross-class reuse at equal tokens.

claim: Without a prompt, people rarely use a stored analogue on a structurally matching but surface-different problem: about 10% base rate, about 30% after memorising the story, about 75-80% once told to use it (Gick and Holyoak 1983).
agent_test: Run O7 on far-class problems with and without a cue naming the source class; count fresh solves.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Spontaneous analogical success is problem-specific and the hint is not a cure: a modern business-problem replication found 6.3% and 20.3% unhinted, 8.7% and 37% hinted (n=46 per cell), below the 1983 rates.
agent_test: Measure hint lift per problem pair, not a pooled rate; expect wide spread.

claim: The bottleneck is noticing, not storage or understanding: a diagram or stated principle added to a single story did not raise unaided use, and the hint fixed most of the gap.
agent_test: Give the agent the full lesson library in context vs retrieved by code; check whether the model notices without a cue.

claim: Retrieval follows surface similarity, while soundness judgement follows structure: surface matches recalled 52% vs purely relational analogies 7%, but people rate the structural analogy as better.
agent_test: Retrieve lessons in two stages (cheap surface/class match, then structural check by code) vs surface-only; compare reuse precision.
update_note: Gap search: experience-following study supports the mechanism for agents (high input similarity gives high output similarity).

claim: Comparing two cases and writing what they share raises transfer over one case: Gick and Holyoak 45% vs 21% unaided (80% vs 53% total); MBA negotiation 40% vs 22% contingent contracts (N=310).
agent_test: Distil a lesson from two solved instances of a class vs one; test on a third class member.

claim: A stated principle helps only after there are two cases to compare; with a single case it adds nothing (62% vs 40% unaided with two cases; single story about 30% either way).
agent_test: Lesson text with vs without an abstract principle line, single vs paired source cases.

claim: The claim that abstract training transfers better than concrete training did not hold up: original 76% vs 44%, but a 2020 replication (38 per condition) found no abstract advantage on transfer and a concrete advantage in initial learning (95% vs 70%). A 2011 replication split by target domain.
agent_test: Compare worked-concrete vs abstracted lessons at equal tokens; do not assume abstract wins.

claim: Far transfer from general training (working memory, music, chess) shrinks toward zero as control quality rises (music 0.25 passive vs 0.03 active; WM g=0.01 for large studies with treated controls); near transfer stays robust.
agent_test: Not a direct agent test; use as a prior against assuming general practice raises unrelated skills.
update_note: Gap search: full text of Sala 2019 read. Far g=0.12 (k=119, CI 0.08-0.16) naive, about 0.01 after placebo and bias control, true variance zero.

claim: Near transfer is reliable inside the trained family (WM training g=0.80 vs treated controls in one meta-analysis, 0.44-0.46 in another), though the size differs between meta-analyses.
agent_test: Reuse lessons within a problem class first; measure the within-class lift at equal tokens.
update_note: Gap search: published near g=0.32 naive (k=99), 0.21 corrected summary, 0.24 active-control only. The 0.27 seen in search summaries is from a preprint.

claim: LLMs do fine on near analogies but fall to or below chance on far ones: ARN humans 94.1% vs models 39.6% on far analogies; near 97.9% vs 75.0%.
agent_test: Compare O7 on near vs far source problems; require code-checked mapping before accepting.
update_note: Gap search: ARN numbers re-confirmed; 39.6% is the all-model average on far analogies (GPT-4 far,far 57.1; far,near 29.1). No o-series/Claude 4+/Gemini 2.5+ ARN result found. Reasoning models match humans on ConceptARC text accuracy but 27% of o3's correct answers use unintended rules. Stays established for 2023-era models; status for current reasoning models unknown.

claim: Whether LLMs reason analogically in an abstract way is contested: GPT-3 matched or beat students on original forms (Webb 2023), but models fell on altered alphabets (humans 0.753 vs GPT-4 0.452) and counterfactual tasks.
agent_test: Test O7 on held-out surface re-skins of the same structure; a gain that vanishes on re-skins is memorisation.

claim: Unfamiliar surface form hurts models much more than humans: adults stay near 0.89-0.91 across alphabets, children 0.62-0.67, GPT-4o 0.85 to 0.48.
agent_test: Mutate surface features of a lesson's source problem and check whether reuse survives.

claim: Near-surface distractors with the wrong structure wreck models: far analogy against a near distractor scored 33.9% for models vs 91.4% for humans; GPT-4 reuse errors in a business test came from surface similarity (precision about 0.5).
agent_test: Add a distractor lesson with matching surface and wrong structure; require a code check before reuse.

claim: Letting the model write its own analogous examples gives modest gains: GSM8K GPT-3.5 75.8 to 77.8, davinci-003 50.3 to 61.0, MATH 33.9 to 37.3; the method needs scale (curie 2%, davinci-002 48%).
agent_test: Self-generated analogues vs plain CoT at equal tokens; count the cost of generating them.

claim: Even relevant, correct self-generated exemplars often fail: of 50 failures, 28 had relevant correct exemplars yet the answer was wrong (12 labelled generalization gap), so mapping, not retrieval, is a second bottleneck.
agent_test: Log the mapping step separately; require code to check the mapping.

claim: Solved demonstrations help far analogies (about +10 points for GPT-3.5 and Llama-2) but cost near-analogy accuracy; GPT-4 was most stable.
agent_test: Gate demonstrations on a distance estimate; test near vs far.

claim: Agents that store abstracted lessons or workflows gain on related tasks: AWM +51.1% relative on WebArena, ExpeL ALFWorld 40 to 59, ReasoningBank +8.3/+7.2/+4.6 over memory-free, Voyager library faster and reused in a new world. Gains are reported by different labs on different benchmarks, not at equal tokens.
agent_test: Lesson store on vs off at equal tokens, within-class and cross-class; we must remeasure.
update_note: Gap search: gains also seen on cross-domain stores (MTL +3.7 points GPT-5-mini) and zero-shot new tasks (LifeMem +18.8 to +22.5% relative, GPT-4o-mini). Gains shrink for stronger backbones.

claim: Abstraction into slots matters more as the domain gap grows: Mind2Web cross-domain step success 18.6 baseline vs 32.6 offline and 35.5 online workflows (cross-task 36.2 vs 45.1 and 43.6).
agent_test: Lessons with placeholders vs literal values, scored on near vs far held-out classes.
update_note: Gap search: AWM Mind2Web step SR gains +8.9 (cross-task), +3.6 (cross-website), +14.0 (cross-domain), but full-task SR stays 0.7-4.8%, so the claim holds only at step level and is not monotonic in distance.

claim: An explicit cue or compare step fixes noticing in LLMs: GPT-4 used the radiation analogy for the factory problem in 1 of 15 unhinted runs and 15 of 15 hinted; recall near 1.0, precision about 0.5 when asked to match.
agent_test: Force a compare-with-library step by code, then measure precision of reuse; false matches are the cost.

claim: Training-time transfer of reasoning is contested: math SFT often failed to transfer (other reasoning 30.2 base, 45.3 SFT, 60.0 RL), yet verified long-CoT SFT on Qwen3-14B raised MATH500 77.8 to 95.1 and GPQA-D 44.1 to 63.3.
agent_test: Outside our scope (no training); a warning that transfer depends on data quality.

claim: Procedural traces from a toy game (Countdown long-CoT) improved math, code and science scores on strong models (AIME24 14.7 to 41.7).
agent_test: Not testable without training.

claim: Barnett and Ceci's nine-dimension taxonomy argues a single far-transfer effect size is misguided; transfer depends on content, context and the gap between learning and use.
agent_test: Report lesson reuse by distance bucket (same class, sibling class, other domain), not one pooled rate.
update_note: Gap search: full Barnett and Ceci text could not be opened (closed access). Stays single-source, abstract only.

claim: Two-stage retrieval, a cheap surface pass then structural match on a few survivors, reproduces human retrieval bias and is cheap enough to run over memory (MAC/FAC, 36-story simulation).
agent_test: Implement MAC/FAC-style lesson retrieval in code; compare with embedding-only retrieval.

claim: For LLM agents, abstracted lessons (insights, skills) transfer more safely across task classes than raw trajectories: Memory Transfer Learning insight +3.7 vs trajectory +1.1 average points over zero-shot (GPT-5-mini); ALFWorld A to B raw -9.5 vs insight +6.5 points; LifeMem raw-trace baselines fell below no-memory on tau-bench airline (0.26 vs 0.32). Differences are small and not token-matched.
agent_test: Store each lesson as a principle line plus a precondition; compare against the full worked trace at equal tokens on a cross-class split.

claim: A lesson store built on other task classes lifts a current small model by a few points: GPT-5-mini +3.7 average Pass@3 over zero-shot across six coding benchmarks (up to +8.3 on MLGym, 0.0 on Aider-Polyglot); DeepSeek V3.2 +2.6, Qwen3-Coder +1.8. Gain grows with pool size and number of source domains.
agent_test: Run a held-out-class lesson test: lessons from classes A-C, test on D, token-matched against a no-lesson control.

claim: Reuse of surface-similar but structurally wrong memory costs real accuracy: raw-trajectory negative transfer up to -26.1 points on baseline-fail items (ALFWorld), -12.7 (BabyAI); baselines below no-memory in LifeMem (-0.06 airline); MTL names domain-mismatched anchoring and false validation confidence; agents copy the most similar stored case. Harm to items the plain model already solved is small (at most -2 points in the one study that splits it).
agent_test: Require a stated precondition check before applying any stored lesson; log cases where lesson-on beats lesson-off and the reverse.

claim: Model-judged lesson selection did not beat plain embedding retrieval: LLM reranking 0.598 and LLM rewriting 0.608 vs embedding similarity 0.630 (no memory 0.584), GPT-5-mini. A code-checked typed mapping has not been tested.
agent_test: Compare embedding, LLM-judge and typed-mapping gates on precision of reuse and tokens per accepted match.

claim: Accuracy on abstraction tests can overstate competence: o3 reaches 77.1% on text ConceptARC (humans 73.0%) but about 27% of its correct outputs rest on unintended or incorrect rules vs about 7% for humans; Claude Sonnet 4 60.2%, Gemini 2.5 Pro 66.0%.
agent_test: When the agent claims an analogy, require it to state the mapping and check the mapping, not only the answer.

claim: The lift from stored experience shrinks as the backbone gets stronger: LifeMem GPT-4o-mini 28.84 to 44.13 (+15.3) vs DeepSeek-v3.2-exp 41.14 to 48.02 (+6.9).
agent_test: Expect a modest lesson-reuse lift for a frontier model; measure before building a large store.
